Weights

Each slider sets how much a criterion counts inside its score. Every company is rescored from its saved evidence as you move them, across the map, the table, the shortlist and the profiles. Your settings stay in this browser only; the published scores do not change.

Methodology

Companies first pass a set of deal-breakers, then get four scores out of 100. A company needs — or more on quality and likelihood to sell to count as high; growth upside ranks companies within each group. Every point carries its source, and an unknown criterion gets half its points. Years in business, founder in charge and no successor together add at most 45 of the 100 likelihood points. A company that would be Pursue now with under 40% of its points sourced goes to Needs research.

What counts as supply chain

Businesses whose product is the supply chain service itself: trucking, final-mile delivery, courier, freight brokerage, 3PL and fulfillment, contract and cold storage, moving and storage, and reverse logistics. Cold chain food distributors also count when perishables move on their own refrigerated fleet or through their own cold storage. Distributors and dealers that mainly resell products are screened out.

Deal-breakers

  • Already owned by private equity or a larger company
  • One customer above 40% of revenue
  • The owner holds the key relationships or licenses with no way to hand them over
  • Franchise, single-platform contractor (such as an Amazon delivery partner) or pure real estate
  • Unsatisfactory federal safety rating, or out-of-service rates far above national averages with serious crashes
  • Sells products (a distributor or dealer) rather than supply chain services or cold chain food distribution

Sources and limits

Company list
The SBA's public PPP loan data (2020–21) for 20 counties within about two hours of Tampa, plus a second pass for warehousing, 3PL, fulfillment and cold storage firms with 8–19 employees, companies whose names say warehouse, logistics or fulfillment under any industry code, and Labor Dept. retirement-plan filers with warehouse or 3PL business codes.
Research
Company websites and their archived history, federal trucking safety and licensing records, county property records for the business site, news and trade press, job postings, reviews and the Better Business Bureau. No one was contacted.
Public records
Labor Department Form 5500 retirement-plan filings (plan years 2024–25) for recent headcount and how long a plan has run; payroll implied by the 2020 SBA loan for a size band. Owner signals count only when an exact quote was found on a public page and re-checked against that page.
Not yet included
Florida business registry filing dates and officers (the state's bulk file was not reachable). Some names come from data-aggregator profiles and need checking before outreach.
